title: The Mistakes That Cost Investors $1.3 MILLION
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
summary: A host-led compilation by Joseph Hogue built around interviews with four investing experts - Jaspreet Singh, Marko (WhiteBoard Finance), Mark Roussin, and Kieran (Fintech Channel) - on the three mistakes that destroy wealth: (1) panic selling and buying hype without a thesis (borrowed conviction becomes borrowed reasons to sell); (2) market timing and turning investing into a casino, backed by Dalbar data showing the average investor's 7% vs the S&P 500's 10.6% compounding to a ~$1.3M gap over 30 years; (3) 'YouTube made me do it' - buying dips and cliches ('buy low, sell high') without doing the homework. Mark Roussin's segment is philosophical, not stock-specific: never buy a stock just because it's down 15-20% - it may be cheap for a reason (margin compression, slowing sales, rising expenses); he screens quality first and valuation second, judging what the company is doing today, not its past glory. Hogue adds his own 5-minute stock framework and anecdotes (doubling down on SMCI at ~$20 after a 33% March crash). Tickers appear only as examples (SMCI, MU/STX/WDC/SNDK, NVDA vs AMD, NKE/AAPL). No explicit stock recommendations from the watched creator; captions clean.
